title.narrative: 2.1 Indicator to outcome 2. Training for HCFs multidisciplinary rehabilitation teams delivered based on needs assessment

description.narrative: 2.1 Indicator to outcome 2. Training for HCFs multidisciplinary rehabilitation teams delivered based on needs assessment

comment.narrative: Lack of educated healthcare professionals from the multidisciplinary rehabilitation teams
Multidisciplinary rehabilitation teams from not less than 5 HCFs covered with education

5 intensive 3day trainings on Interdisciplinary Approach to Rehabilitation Services Provision were held for 75 individual specialists in the field of rehabilitation. After completing these trainings the specialists improved their knowledge and skills in the regulatory framework for the work of a multidisciplinary team psychological aspects of the rehabilitation process and the specifics of physical and occupational therapy for patients with musculoskeletal and nervous system injuries. They also developed skills in using various scales and tests to assess the condition of patients after injuries considered the specifics of cardio and neurorehabilitation and many other topics. Based on the results of the training all specialists were tested and received CPD points. We received very positive feedback from all participants. Their knowledge has become more structured and deeper. All expressed a desire to continue training to develop their professional expertise. One 1day training on Effective communication was held for 14 individual specialists.Within this training specialists improved communication skills between medical staff rehabilitation specialists and patients to achieve a highquality and effective rehabilitation process. All participants expressed the importance of bringing this topic to a wider range of professionals.

comment.narrative: Lack of educated healthcare professionals from the multidisciplinary rehabilitation teams
Multidisciplinary rehabilitation teams from not less than 5 HCFs covered with education

5 intensive 3day trainings on Interdisciplinary Approach to Rehabilitation Services Provision were held for 75 individual specialists in the field of rehabilitation. After completing these trainings the specialists improved their knowledge and skills in the regulatory framework for the work of a multidisciplinary team psychological aspects of the rehabilitation process and the specifics of physical and occupational therapy for patients with musculoskeletal and nervous system injuries. They also developed skills in using various scales and tests to assess the condition of patients after injuries considered the specifics of cardio and neurorehabilitation and many other topics. Based on the results of the training all specialists were tested and received CPD points. We received very positive feedback from all participants. Their knowledge has become more structured and deeper. All expressed a desire to continue training to develop their professional expertise. One 1day training on Effective communication was held for 14 individual specialists.Within this training specialists improved communication skills between medical staff rehabilitation specialists and patients to achieve a highquality and effective rehabilitation process. All participants expressed the importance of bringing this topic to a wider range of professionals.

comment.narrative: Not less than 5 HCFs are reached

The workshop Strategy for the Development of a Rehabilitation Department as a Part of a Hospital was held on November 34 in Dnipro at the City Clinical Hospital No. 4 of the Dnipro City Council. Management teams from 10 healthcare facilities HCFs from different regions of Ukraine were selected to participate in the event. Those teams that are motivated and ready to implement new knowledge and skills to improve the work of their rehabilitation departments were identified. Day 1 of the event was devoted to studying the hospitals experience in the development and functioning of their rehabilitation department City Clinical Hospital No. 4 of the Dnipro City Council one of the centres of excellence in Ukraine identified by the Ministry of Health of Ukraine.Day 2 of the event was devoted to studying the issues of the rehabilitation departments effective work and sharing the participants experience with further planning of the development stages.As a result of the event the 5 most active and motivated teams were selected to receive supervision from experienced rehabilitation experts for 3 months to implement their rehabilitation department development plans. The supervision is currently ongoing until the end of February 2024.

Management teams from 10 healthcare facilities HCFs from different regions of Ukraine were selected to participate in the event. Those teams that are motivated and ready to implement new knowledge and skills to improve the work of their rehabilitation departments were identified. Day 1 of the event was devoted to studying the hospitals experience in the development and functioning of their rehabilitation department City Clinical Hospital No. 4 of the Dnipro City Council one of the centres of excellence in Ukraine identified by the Ministry of Health of Ukraine.Day 2 of the event was devoted to studying the issues of the rehabilitation departments effective work and sharing the participants experience with further planning of the development stages.As a result of the event the 5 most active and motivated teams were selected to receive supervision from experienced rehabilitation experts for 3 months to implement their rehabilitation department development plans. The supervision is currently ongoing until the end of February 2024.
